basis: Inherited erythroid marrow failure; skeletal anomalies lack a reliable frequency here, while specified renal and cardiac defects are occasional.
Congenital abdominal wall defect; pulmonary hypoplasia and restrictive dysfunction occur in 30-79%. Herniated viscera do not establish intrinsic organ damage.
Microcephaly and profound developmental impairment define the disorder; selected 1-3-patient reports do not establish common extracerebral damage across 21 cases.
Inherited glycogen metabolism disorder; hepatic, skeletal muscle and cardiac damage depend on subtype and are not shared across this broad umbrella.
Defining eyelid malformations and dental agenesis affect 3/3; cleft lip affects 2/3. Cutaneous syndactyly is very rare.
Reflex autonomic spells with transient breath cessation and sometimes syncope; no persistent pulmonary or cardiac damage is established.
Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and ataxia; strabismus affects 11/13. Dysphagia alone does not establish gastrointestinal tissue damage.
Optic atrophy 3/3; pancreatic insufficiency and posterior urethral valve each reported once in this three-case disorder (~33%). ASD and arthrogryposis omitted by cap.
Optic atrophy, hearing loss and peripheral neuropathy are the defining disease triad.
Mitochondrial energy disorder; developmental impairment 2/3, cardiomyopathy/heart failure 1/3 and retinal degeneration 1/3. Gallstones are a separate disease.
Viral infection umbrella; respiratory, salivary gland and neurologic disease vary by virus, without a consistently shared damaged organ.
Localized cutaneous mast-cell proliferation forming plaques; systemic marrow or other organ infiltration is not established by this concept.
Congenital defect of the skeletal-muscle diaphragm; pulmonary hypoplasia is not established as common in the anterior subtype.
Viral infection directly inflames liver parenchyma; no extrahepatic damage is consistently common across viral hepatitis types.
Inherited cerebral white-matter degeneration with progressive neurologic deterioration in 4/4.
Parkinsonism and pyramidal tract dysfunction define the disorder; spasticity reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than primary muscle disease.
Meningioma arising within the brainstem; glycogen-rich tumour cells do not imply systemic metabolic disease.
Defining intellectual and speech impairment; strabismus occurs in 30-79%. Genitourinary findings lack renal specificity; recurrent otitis is a separate infection.
Paraprotein-associated immune-mediated polyradiculoneuropathy; the accompanying monoclonal gammopathy does not establish blood or marrow damage.
Hearing loss, eyelid dysfunction/keratitis and RBBB each annotated 30-79%; retinal vascular changes may not impair vision. Restriction reflects respiratory muscle weakness.
Pathologic distention and impaired function of the stomach; underlying causes do not establish additional affected organs.
Infectious corneal ulcer with hypopyon; ancestry identifies infectious anterior ocular inflammation.
Immune-mediated destruction of sensory ganglion neurons, commonly anti-Hu associated; the triggering malignancy is a separate disease.
Inherited atrial electrical dysfunction; stroke reported in 3/6 is a separately diagnosed thromboembolic complication and is excluded.
Inherited epilepsy syndrome with febrile and generalized or focal seizures; no additional organ damage is established.
